extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners handling ex parte appeals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing an examiner's answer in an ex parte appeal, including when and how to assert new grounds of rejection, required approvals, form-paragraph structure, timing, and how to treat amendments, evidence, and appellant arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete explanation for each new ground of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: For each new ground of rejection, a complete explanation supporting the rejection must be provided with a proper reference to the applicable statute, prior art references relied upon, and the claim numbers of the claims that are subject to the rejection in the examiner’s answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New grounds must include statute citation, cited references, and claim numbers; must be prominently identified in the 'Grounds of Rejection to be Reviewed on Appeal' section under 'New Grounds of Rejection' (may use form paragraph 12.256).

rubrics_metrics.name: Response to Argument
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement of whether the examiner disagrees with each of the arguments of appellant in the brief with respect to the issues presented and an explanation of the reasons for disagreement with any such argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner must use headings and subheadings paralleling the headings and subheadings utilized in the appellant’s brief. If an issue was fully responded to in the 'Grounds of Rejection to be Reviewed on Appeal' portion, no additional response is required; otherwise a full response must be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of examiner's answer
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should furnish the appellant with a written statement in answer to the appellant’s brief within 2 months after the receipt of the brief by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 41.39(a) states the examiner 'may' furnish an answer, but current procedures do not permit an appeal to proceed to the Board without an examiner's answer. The mailing date of the examiner's answer begins the period for filing a reply brief, the time to request an oral hearing, and the period for payment of the appeal forwarding fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplified answer when final rejection fully addresses arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: If the final rejection fully addresses the arguments in the appeal brief, the examiner should complete an examiner's answer with a typical 'Grounds of Rejection to be Reviewed on Appeal' section and a simplified 'Response to Arguments' section that simply refers to the appropriate portion of the final rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a concise response referencing the final rejection rather than repeating material when the final rejection already addresses the brief's arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicate entry/non-entry of after-final amendments and advisory action
rubrics_metrics.description: Before preparing the answer, the examiner should make certain that each after-final amendment or evidence has been indicated as being entered or not-entered and an advisory action has been entered for each after-final amendment or evidence to notify the appellant of the entry or non-entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board may remand applications in which after-final amendment or evidence has not been indicated as entered or not-entered and acted upon in an advisory action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of affidavits, declarations, and exhibits filed with notice of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should treat affidavits, declarations, or exhibits filed with the notice of appeal in accordance with 37 CFR 1.116; if an affidavit, declaration, or exhibit was refused entry in the Record under 37 CFR 1.116 or prohibited by 37 CFR 41.33, the examiner should not comment on it in the examiner’s answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It would be improper for appellant to rely on an affidavit, declaration, or exhibit which was not entered. If appellant has grounds for challenging non-entry, they should file a timely petition under 37 CFR 1.181. Affidavits or declarations swearing behind a reference should be clearly identified as being considered under 37 CFR 1.131.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation requirement for non-English documents relied upon
rubrics_metrics.description: If a document being relied upon by the examiner in support of a rejection is in a language other than English, a translation must be obtained so that the record is clear as to the precise facts the examiner is relying upon in support of the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The translation may be a machine translation or an English equivalent of the non-English document. See MPEP § 2120 for reliance upon abstracts and foreign language documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presume all rejected claims are on appeal; maintain rejections unless overcome
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners are not to make any determination whether fewer than all of the rejected claims are identified by the appellant as being appealed. The Board will presume that all of the rejected claims are on appeal; therefore, the examiner will treat all pending, rejected claims as being on appeal, and maintain all of the rejections set forth in the Office action from which the appeal is taken, unless appellant has overcome the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appellant can overcome by persuasive arguments, acceptable terminal disclaimer, or evidence. If appellant requested abeyance or did not present argument on a rejection in the brief, the examiner should maintain the rejection and identify that the appellant has not argued it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify treatment of claims amended or added for appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an amendment under 37 CFR 1.116 or 41.33 would be entered for appeal purposes, the examiner must identify (in an advisory action) how one or more individual rejections set forth in the final rejection would be used to reject the added or amended claim(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the advisory action indicates which individual rejections would be used, the appeal brief must address the rejection(s) of the added/ amended claims and the examiner's answer may include those rejections (and such rejections would not be considered new grounds of rejection).

rubrics_metrics.name: Expressly withdraw rejections not adhered to and note claim status changes
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should reevaluate their position in light of the arguments presented in the brief, and should expressly withdraw any rejections not adhered to in the 'WITHDRAWN REJECTIONS' subsection of the examiner’s answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner withdraws all rejections of an independent claim, the answer should note the change of status and include changes to dependent claims. If a dependent claim's rejections are withdrawn while the independent claim is maintained, applicant may file an amendment under 37 CFR 41.33(b)(2) rewriting the claims in independent form. If the independent claim is affirmed on appeal, the amendment to rewrite must be presented before expiration of the period set in 37 CFR 90.3.

rubrics_metrics.name: New ground of rejection allowed but supervisory approval required to reopen prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: A new ground of rejection is permitted in an examiner’s answer. If reopening of prosecution is necessary, the examiner must obtain approval from the supervisory patent examiner prior to reopening prosecution after an appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§ 1002.02(d) and 1207.04 for reopening procedure and supervisory approval requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval and prominence requirements for new grounds of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Any new ground of rejection made by an examiner in an answer must be approved by a Technology Center (TC) Director or designee and prominently identified in the 'Grounds of Rejection to be Reviewed on Appeal' section under the subheading 'New Grounds of Rejection'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner's answer must include the signature of the TC Director or designee to indicate approval. Form paragraph 12.256 may be used to introduce new grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide two-month reply period and state appellant's options for new grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner’s answer must provide appellant a two-month time period for reply and notify appellant of the reply period and options following the new grounds of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appellant must either (A) reopen prosecution by filing a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 (with or without amendment, affidavit or other evidence) or (B) maintain the appeal by filing a reply brief addressing each new ground in compliance with 37 CFR 41.37(c)(1)(iv). Use form paragraph 12.279.01 to notify of the two-month period and include TC Director approval. Extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) do not apply to this two-month period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for failure to timely reply to new grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: If appellant fails to file the required reply under 37 CFR 1.111 or a reply brief within the two-month period required by 37 CFR 41.39, the appeal as to the claims subject to the new ground of rejection may be dismissed and those claims canceled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 12.279.02 to document dismissal and to insert the relevant claim numbers and mailing dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation as new ground when evidence is applied or cited for first time
rubrics_metrics.description: If evidence (such as a new prior art reference, but not including a newly relied upon dictionary definition) is applied or cited for the first time in an examiner's answer, then 37 CFR 41.39(a)(2) requires that the rejection be designated as a new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If citation of a new prior art reference is necessary to support a rejection, it must be included in the statement of rejection and designated as a new ground; even minor reliance should be positively included. See MPEP § 2144.03 for guidance on citation of new references for Official Notice in Office actions made prior to an examiner's answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: New grounds are not permissible against previously allowed or objected-to claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A new ground of rejection would not be permitted to reject a previously allowed or objected-to claim even if the new ground of rejection would rely upon evidence already of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In such cases, the examiner should reopen prosecution (with supervisory approval) rather than make a new ground of rejection in the examiner’s answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion for when a ground of rejection is 'new' — change in basic thrust or new facts/rationales
rubrics_metrics.description: A position or rationale that changes the 'basic thrust of the rejection' will give rise to a new ground of rejection. A rejection relying on the same statutory basis and same prior art references may still be new if it relies on new facts or rationales not previously raised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different language or restatement of reasoning alone does not necessarily create a new ground so long as the basic thrust is the same and appellant has had a fair opportunity to respond (see In re Kronig and related case law). The ultimate criterion is whether appellants have had fair opportunity to react to the thrust of the rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example: change of statutory basis 35 U.S.C. 102 ↔ 35 U.S.C. 103 constitutes a new ground
rubrics_metrics.description: Changing the statutory basis of rejection from 35 U.S.C. 102 to 35 U.S.C. 103, or vice versa based on a different teaching, should be designated as a new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case law (e.g., In re Hughes; In re Echerd) supports that changing the statutory section or relying on a different portion/teaching of a reference calls for a new ground because it may require different evidence or rebuttal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example: new calculations, structures, or portions relied upon can create new grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Citing new calculations (e.g., overlapping ranges identified/calculated for the first time), citing a different structure in support of structural obviousness, or pointing to a different portion of a reference or claim limitation may create a new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such factual additions or reliance on different facts/portions that alter the basis/facts supporting a rejection have been held to constitute new grounds (e.g., In re Kumar; In re Wiechert; In re Waymouth).

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations not considered new grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no new ground of rejection when the basic thrust of the rejection remains the same such that an appellant has been given a fair opportunity to react; a change in discussion or rationale without new evidence or new statutory basis does not necessarily constitute a new ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific non-new examples include: citing a different portion of a reference to elaborate upon previously cited material; rejections applied to claims added/amended under 37 CFR 1.116/41.33 when advisory action indicated which individual rejections would apply (applicant was advised); and use of references merely to support what was already asserted as 'well-known' in the art (see MPEP § 2144.03).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraphs and required structure in examiner's answer
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner's answer should follow established form-paragraph structure (e.g., ¶12.249 Examiner’s Answer Cover Sheet; ¶12.254 Grounds of Rejection to be Reviewed on Appeal; ¶12.255 Restatement of Rejection; ¶12.256 New Grounds of Rejection - Heading; ¶12.257 Withdrawn Rejections; ¶12.261 Response to Argument; ¶12.279 Conclusion/¶12.279.01 Conclusion raising new grounds; ¶12.279.02 Dismissal following new grounds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the specified form paragraphs where applicable, populate bracketed fields appropriately (dates, claim numbers, conferees, signatures), and follow examiner notes on when to use particular paragraphs and insertions (e.g., when notice of appeal filed on or after January 23, 2012). Conclude answers containing new grounds with form paragraph 12.279.01 to notify applicant of reply period and include required TC Director approval.
